newsitem.title: USA: CME HOGS END OFF SHARPLY, PORK BELLIES MIXED.
newsitem.headline: CME HOGS END OFF SHARPLY, PORK BELLIES MIXED.

text.p: CME hog futures remained pressured from technical and fundamental factors to close sharply lower while pork bellies ended mixed with August up on tight deliverable supplies, traders said.

Hog futures ended 1.225 to 0.250 cents per lb lower with October off most at 72.700 cents. Pork bellies ended 1.375 higher to 0.950 lower with August up most at 87.900 and February off 0.400 at 75.150 cents.
Hog futures eased to lowest price levels in two weeks on renewed fund and speculative liquidation prompted by weak cash markets and seasonal considerations, traders said.

Cooler temperatures allowed increased hog marketings and the increased pace of slaughter is pressuring pork product values. Disappointment over the lighter than expected pace of pork exports s adding to weakness, they said.
"The cash market is going to come down starting now into the first week of September or so, which is seasonal and traditional," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron trading Corp.
Levitt said the market was taking note of the seasonal break and the only thing that could countrer that would have been an increase in export business or domestic demand.

Rand Financials bought August while E.D.&F. Man and RBH sold. LIT division of First Options, Cargill Investor Services, Rosenthal Collins and LIT sold October. In hog options, LFG bought December 64 puts and Iowa Grain was actively liquidating August 82 calls, pit sources sais.

August bellies remained higher in thin trade on support generated by expectations cash bellies will only show a small setback before rising again and concern deliverable stock is already in strong hands. Next year contracts were mostly technical in nature and are expected to remain that way until October, traders said.
"There is pressure on the (cash belly) market but it feels like down around 87 or 88 cents the market will have some support," Levitt said.
"Most of the deliverable quality bellies that are around are already in strong hands," he added.
LFG bought August after early support from R.J. O'Brien. LIT division of First Options bought August and sold February while Dean Witter sold February, pit sources said.
